title: Facility Engineer (m/w/d)
description:
Unternehmensprofil

nLighten ist eine europäische Plattform für verteilte Edge-Rechenzentren, die auf den wachsenden Bedarf an KI, 5G und hybriden Cloud-Lösungen ausgerichtet ist. Als schnell wachsender Anbieter bieten wir skalierbare Colocation-Sites und fortschrittlichste Energielösungen in ganz Europa. Unser innovativer und nachhaltiger Ansatz für digitale, souveräne Infrastruktur sorgt für Zuverlässigkeit, Effizienz und langfristige Lösungen für unsere Kunden.
nLighten betreibt derzeit 34 Rechenzentren in 7 europäischen Ländern und plant, sein Netzwerk in den nächsten 3 bis 4 Jahren auf 100 Standorte auszubauen.
Mehr über uns: www.nlighten.com

Über die Rolle

Für unseren Standort in Stuttgart suchen wir einen erfahrenen Facility Engineer (m/w/d) mit mehrjähriger praktischer Erfahrung im Rechenzentrumsbetrieb. In dieser Rolle verantwortest Du den störungsfreien Betrieb unserer technischen Infrastruktur vor Ort, koordinierst Wartungs- und Ausbauarbeiten und unterstützt Kunden bei komplexen Installationen und technischen Anforderungen.

Deine Aufgaben

• Vor Ort Betriebsführung der Rechenzentrumsinfrastruktur

• Stromversorgung sicherstellen

• Betrieb und Überwachung der Mittel- und Niederspannungsanlagen

• Betreuung von Transformatoren

• Betrieb von USV-Anlagen (unterbrechungsfreie Stromversorgung)

• Betrieb von Notstromgeneratoren

• Durchführung von Lasttests und Umschaltungen

• Kühlung und Klimatisierung

• Überwachung der Kälteanlagen

• Betrieb von CRAC-/CRAH-Systemen

• Kontrolle von Temperatur und Luftfeuchtigkeit

• Optimierung der Energieeffizienz (PUE)

• Gebäudetechnik (Building Management)

• Arbeiten mit Building Management Systems (BMS)

• Kontrolle von Sensoren, Alarmen und Automatisierungssystemen

• Überwachung technischer Anlagen

• Netzwerkinfrastruktur LWL, Cat6/7

• Verkabelung

• Messung

• Fehlersuche

• Sauberes Kabelmanagement

• Dokumentation und Beschriftung

• Wartung und Störungsmanagement

• Planung und Durchführung von Wartungen

• Koordination externer Dienstleister

• Fehleranalyse bei technischen Störungen (Root-Cause)

• Erstellung von Notfallmaßnahmen (EOPs)

• Sorgfältige Dokumentation aller Einsätze, Störungen & Vorfälle

• Sicherheit und Risiko-Management

• Brandschutzsysteme überwachen

• Durchführung von Notfallübungen

• Einhaltung aller Sicherheits-, Gesundheits- und Betriebsprozesse

• Unterstützung von Audits und Zertifizierungen

• Change Management

• Bewertung von technischen Änderungen

• Erstellung von MOPs (Method of Procedure)

• Erstellung von PtWs

• Erstellung von Risk Assessments

• Durchführung von geplanten Umschaltungen

• Risikobewertung vor Eingriffen

• Kundeninfrastruktur

• Ausführen und Betrieb von Kundeninstallationen

• Ausführen von Cross-Connects

• Remote Hands & Troubleshooting

• Dokumentation

• Vendor-Management

• Einholen von Angeboten

• Einhaltung von Budgets prüfen

• Einweisung vor Ort

• Kontrolle der Abschlussberichte

• Teilnahme an einer Rufbereitschaftsrotation für dringende technische Einsätze

• Enge Zusammenarbeit mit dem Operations Regional Manager & dem Operations-Team

Das bringst Du mit

• Abgeschlossene technische Berufsausbildung, z. B. Elektriker, Mechatroniker, Kältetechniker oder eine vergleichbare Fachrichtung

• Weiterbildung zum Techniker oder Meister ist wünschenswert

• Bereitschaft zur Ernennung zur Elektrofachkraft, sowie passende Qualifikation

• Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Rechenzentrumsbetrieb oder in einer vergleichbaren technischen Umgebung

• Technisches Know-how im Bereich Elektro/Mechanik & IT-Connectivity

• Lösungsorientiertes Denken und die Fähigkeit, Probleme unter Druck zu lösen

• Grundkenntnisse in Netzwerken, Verkabelung und Fehlersuche

• Strukturierte Arbeitsweise, saubere Dokumentation & organisatorisches Talent

• Du arbeitest gerne selbstständig, aber auch im Team

• Deutsch oder Englisch fließend – beides ist ein Plus

Warum nLighten?

• Wachstum & Perspektive: Wir expandieren stark und bieten Chancen für Entwicklung – fachlich wie karriereseitig

• Mitgestalten: Du hältst unseren Standort am Laufen und hast direkten Impact auf Kundenzufriedenheit & Betriebsstabilität

• Zukunftsbranche: Arbeite in einem Umfeld, das AI-, Cloud- und 5G-Infrastruktur der nächsten Generation ermöglicht

Klingt spannend?

Dann freuen wir uns auf Deine Bewerbung!
Werde Teil unserer Mission – für eine vernetzte, effiziente und nachhaltige digitale Zukunft.

Hintergrundprüfung & Screening

Alle ausgewählten Kandidat:innen durchlaufen eine Hintergrundprüfung, um ein sicheres Arbeitsumfeld zu gewährleisten, Unternehmenswerte zu schützen und den gesetzlichen Anforderungen zu entsprechen.

Vielfalt & Inklusion

nLighten steht für Chancengleichheit. Wir fördern ein diverses Arbeitsumfeld und freuen uns über Bewerbungen jeder Herkunft, jedes Geschlechts und jeder Identität – auch wenn Du nicht alle Kriterien erfüllst, freuen wir uns über Deine Bewerbung – insbesondere ermutigen wir Frauen und Menschen aus unterrepräsentierten Gruppen, sich bei uns zu bewerben.

Reporting to the Group Financial Controller, you will ensure statutory accounts are prepared, audited, and filed on time, own the group's audit governance, including the group audit plan, internal audit programme, and Audit Committee process , and manage our outsourced tax providers across Europe to keep nLighten compliant in every market.

This role suits a Big 4 audit-trained accountant who enjoys technical depth and wants broad exposure across reporting and tax in a fast-growing, PE-backed infrastructure business.

Key Responsibilities

Statutory accounting and audit

• Own the annual statutory accounts process for all nLighten entities across all jurisdictions, from planning through to filing

• Manage the group and local statutory audit processes end-to-end: audit planning, deliverables tracking, auditor queries, and issue resolution

• Act as the primary day-to-day contact for external auditors, coordinating input from local finance teams and external service providers

• Maintain the statutory compliance calendar, ensuring all filing deadlines are met in every jurisdiction

Audit planning and governance

• Track audit findings and management actions to closure, reporting status to the Group Financial Controller and Audit Committee

Internal audit and Audit Committee

• Own and run the group's internal audit programme delivered by outsourced providers: developing the risk-based internal audit plan, executing or coordinating reviews, and reporting findings and remediation progress

• Manage the Audit Committee process end-to-end: setting the annual calendar, preparing agendas and papers, coordinating external auditor attendance, and tracking actions arising

• Act as secretary to the Audit Committee, ensuring high-quality minutes and timely follow-up on committee decisions

Technical accounting

• Act as the group's technical accounting resource, providing controllers with clear guidance on the accounting treatment of complex areas — including revenue recognition (IFRS 15) and lease accounting (IFRS 16)

• Prepare technical accounting papers supporting the group's positions on significant judgements and new transactions, for review with the Group Financial Controller and external auditors

• Support the monthly reporting process by resolving technical questions from entity controllers and reviewing the treatment of non-routine transactions

• Maintain and develop the group accounting policy manual, keeping it current with new standards and group developments

Tax compliance

• Manage the group's outsourced tax providers across all jurisdictions, acting as the central point of coordination

• Track adviser recommendations to completion, ensuring nLighten follows up and remains tax compliant in every market

• Oversee the external preparation and filing of annual corporate income tax returns, ensuring the process runs smoothly and deadlines are met

• Coordinate the tax provisioning process for statutory and group reporting, working with advisers and the group finance team

• Maintain oversight of the group's wider tax compliance obligations (including VAT and transfer pricing documentation), escalating risks and issues to the Group Financial Controller

Wider finance team

• Work closely with entity controllers and the group consolidation team to align statutory, tax, and group reporting

• Support the finance integration of newly acquired entities, ensuring statutory and tax compliance obligations are captured from day one

• Contribute to the continuous improvement of reporting processes, templates, and controls

What We Are Looking For

• 10+ years of experience, including approximately 5 years in audit practice and 5 years in industry

• Big 4 audit-trained, qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, RA, or equivalent)

• Strong technical IFRS knowledge, with demonstrable depth in revenue recognition (IFRS 15) and lease accounting (IFRS 16)

• Experience preparing or auditing statutory financial statements for multi-entity, multi-jurisdiction groups

• Experience managing external audit relationships and delivering audits to deadline

• Working knowledge of corporate tax compliance processes and experience coordinating external tax advisers

• Experience building and managing audit plans and reporting audit status to senior stakeholders (board, audit committee, or equivalent)

• Highly organised, with the ability to run parallel workstreams across multiple entities and deadlines

• Clear written and verbal communication, able to translate technical accounting into practical guidance for controllers

• Fluent English

Nice to Have

• Experience in a private equity-backed, leveraged, and/or capex-intensive environment (infrastructure, data centres, real estate)

• Exposure to European statutory reporting regimes and local GAAP to IFRS conversion

• Experience with transfer pricing and cross-border intercompany arrangements

• Internal audit experience, or experience designing and testing financial controls

• Experience supporting or managing an audit committee, including paper preparation and minute-taking

title: Operations Regional Manager (m/w/d)
description:
Unternehmensprofil

nLighten ist eine europäische Plattform für verteilte Edge-Rechenzentren, die auf den wachsenden Bedarf an KI, 5G und hybriden Cloud-Lösungen ausgerichtet ist. Als schnell wachsender Anbieter bieten wir skalierbare Colocation-Sites und fortschrittlichste Energielösungen in ganz Europa. Unser innovativer und nachhaltiger Ansatz für digitale, souveräne Infrastruktur sorgt für Zuverlässigkeit, Effizienz und langfristige Lösungen für unsere Kunden.
nLighten betreibt derzeit 34 Rechenzentren in 7 europäischen Ländern und plant, sein Netzwerk in den nächsten 3 bis 4 Jahren auf 100 Standorte auszubauen.
Mehr über uns: www.nlighten.com

Über die Rolle

Wir suchen einen erfahrenen und strategischen Operations Regional Manager (m/w/d), der die Verantwortung für den effizienten und zuverlässigen Betrieb mehrerer Rechenzentren innerhalb einer zugewiesenen Region in Frankfurt oder Berlin übernimmt. In dieser Rolle stellst Du eine optimale Performance der Standorte sowie die Einhaltung unserer operativen Standards sicher und sorgst dafür, dass der Rechenzentrumsbetrieb im Einklang mit den strategischen Zielen unseres Unternehmens steht. Du bringst ausgeprägte Führungskompetenz, fundierte Erfahrung im operativen Rechenzentrumsbetrieb sowie die Fähigkeit mit, mehrere Standorte und Teams erfolgreich zu steuern.

Deine Aufgaben

• Du verantwortest den täglichen Betrieb mehrerer Rechenzentren und stellst deren Verfügbarkeit, Zuverlässigkeit sowie die Einhaltung der vereinbarten Service Level Agreements (SLAs) sicher.

• Du implementierst und überwachst betriebliche Prozesse und Abläufe und sorgst für eine einheitliche Umsetzung an allen Standorten.

• Du identifizierst und bewertest betriebliche Risiken und entwickelst Notfall- und Maßnahmenpläne, um Betriebsunterbrechungen zu minimieren.

• Du führst und unterstützt die Teams vor Ort, gibst klare Orientierung, förderst die Weiterentwicklung der Mitarbeitenden und stellst eine hohe Servicequalität sicher.

• Du stellst sicher, dass die physische Infrastruktur – insbesondere Stromversorgung, Kühlung und Sicherheitssysteme – entsprechend den betrieblichen Standards gewartet und betrieben wird.

• Du koordinierst und steuerst externe Dienstleister und Auftragnehmer bei Wartungs-, Reparatur- und Ausbauarbeiten.

• Du verantwortest die operativen Budgets, identifizierst Optimierungspotenziale und überwachst relevante Leistungskennzahlen mit Blick auf Effizienz, Kosten und Qualität.

• Du stellst eine korrekte und zeitgerechte Berichterstattung zu KPIs, Kapazitäten und operativen Kennzahlen sicher.

• Gemeinsam mit den zentralen Compliance-Verantwortlichen stellst du die Einhaltung aller relevanten gesetzlichen, regulatorischen und sicherheitsbezogenen Anforderungen im Rechenzentrumsbetrieb sicher.

• Du fungierst als zentraler regionaler Ansprechpartner für Kunden, interne Stakeholder und das zentrale Operations-Team.

• Du bist erster Ansprechpartner für Compliance-Themen und Incident Management sowie die zentrale Schnittstelle zum Construction-Team.

Das bringst Du mit

• Abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich Elektrotechnik, Maschinenbau, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen oder eine vergleichbare technische Qualifikation.

• Mindestens 5 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Betrieb von Rechenzentren oder anderen kritischen Infrastrukturen, davon mindestens 3 Jahre in einer Führungsposition.

• Fundiertes Verständnis kritischer technischer Systeme, insbesondere Stromversorgung, Kühlung, Brandschutz und Building Management Systems (BMS).

• Nachweisbare Erfahrung im Vendor Management, in der Budget- und Kostensteuerung sowie in der Optimierung von Prozessen.

• Ausgeprägte Führungs-, Kommunikations- und Organisationsfähigkeiten.

• Eine hohe Kunden- und Serviceorientierung ist von Vorteil.

• Ausgeprägte Problemlösungskompetenz mit einem starken Fokus auf operative Effizienz.

• Sehr gute Kommunikations- und zwischenmenschliche Fähigkeiten im Umgang mit Teams und unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern.

• Fließende Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse; weitere europäische Sprachen sind von Vorteil.

• Du hast Freude daran, interne Trainings zu organisieren und voranzutreiben und die Operations-Teams für Weiterbildungsangebote zu begeistern.

Warum nLighten?

• Wachstum & Perspektive: Wir expandieren stark und bieten Chancen für Entwicklung – fachlich wie karriereseitig

• Mitgestalten: Du hältst unseren Standort am Laufen und hast direkten Impact auf Kundenzufriedenheit & Betriebsstabilität

• Zukunftsbranche: Arbeite in einem Umfeld, das AI-, Cloud- und 5G-Infrastruktur der nächsten Generation ermöglicht

Klingt spannend?

Dann freuen wir uns auf Deine Bewerbung!
Werde Teil unserer Mission – für eine vernetzte, effiziente und nachhaltige digitale Zukunft.

Hintergrundprüfung & Screening

Alle ausgewählten Kandidat:innen durchlaufen eine Hintergrundprüfung, um ein sicheres Arbeitsumfeld zu gewährleisten, Unternehmenswerte zu schützen und den gesetzlichen Anforderungen zu entsprechen.

Vielfalt & Inklusion

nLighten steht für Chancengleichheit. Wir fördern ein diverses Arbeitsumfeld und freuen uns über Bewerbungen jeder Herkunft, jedes Geschlechts und jeder Identität – auch wenn Du nicht alle Kriterien erfüllst, freuen wir uns über Deine Bewerbung – insbesondere ermutigen wir Frauen und Menschen aus unterrepräsentierten Gruppen, sich bei uns zu bewerben.

description:

title: Site Technician (m/w/d)
description:
Unternehmensprofil

nLighten ist eine europäische Plattform für verteilte Edge-Rechenzentren, die auf den wachsenden Bedarf an KI, 5G und hybriden Cloud-Lösungen ausgerichtet ist. Als schnell wachsender Anbieter bieten wir skalierbare Colocation-Sites und fortschrittlichste Energielösungen in ganz Europa. Unser innovativer und nachhaltiger Ansatz für digitale, souveräne Infrastruktur sorgt für Zuverlässigkeit, Effizienz und langfristige Lösungen für unsere Kunden.
nLighten betreibt derzeit 34 Rechenzentren in 7 europäischen Ländern und plant, sein Netzwerk in den nächsten 3 bis 4 Jahren auf 100 Standorte auszubauen.
Mehr über uns: www.nlighten.com

Über die Rolle

Für unseren Standort in Stuttgart suchen wir einen erfahrenen Site Technician (m/w/d) mit mehrjähriger praktischer Erfahrung im Rechenzentrumsbetrieb. In dieser Rolle verantwortest Du den störungsfreien Betrieb unserer technischen Infrastruktur vor Ort, koordinierst Wartungs- und Ausbauarbeiten und unterstützt Kunden bei komplexen Installationen und technischen Anforderungen.

Deine Aufgaben

• Regelmäßige Inspektionen & präventive Wartung an kritischen Systemen (Strom, Kühlung, BMS)

• Überwachung des BMS, Erkennen von Alarmen & Einleiten technischer Maßnahmen

• Unterstützung bei Kundeninstallationen, Cross-Connects, Remote Hands & Troubleshooting

• Sauberes Kabelmanagement, korrekte Beschriftung & Dokumentation aller Aktivitäten

• Koordination externer Dienstleister & Überwachung von Wartungs- und Reparaturarbeiten

• Angebote einholen, Budgets prüfen & Abschlussberichte kontrollieren

• Sorgfältige Dokumentation aller Einsätze, Störungen & Vorfälle

• Teilnahme an einer Rufbereitschaftsrotation für dringende technische Einsätze

• Einhaltung aller Sicherheits-, Gesundheits- und Betriebsprozesse

• Enge Zusammenarbeit mit dem Data Center Lead & dem Operations-Team

Das bringst Du mit

• Abgeschlossene technische Berufsausbildung, z. B. Elektriker, Mechatroniker, Kältetechniker oder eine vergleichbare Fachrichtung

• Weiterbildung zum Techniker oder Meister ist wünschenswert

• Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Rechenzentrumsbetrieb oder in einer vergleichbaren technischen Umgebung

• Technisches Know-how im Bereich Elektro/Mechanik & IT-Connectivity

• Lösungsorientiertes Denken und die Fähigkeit, Probleme unter Druck zu lösen

• Grundkenntnisse in Netzwerken, Verkabelung und Fehlersuche

• Strukturierte Arbeitsweise, saubere Dokumentation & organisatorisches Talent

• Du arbeitest gerne selbstständig, aber auch im Team

• Deutsch oder Englisch fließend – beides ist ein Plus

Warum nLighten?

• Wachstum & Perspektive: Wir expandieren stark und bieten Chancen für Entwicklung – fachlich wie karriereseitig

• Mitgestalten: Du hältst unseren Standort am Laufen und hast direkten Impact auf Kundenzufriedenheit & Betriebsstabilität

• Zukunftsbranche: Arbeite in einem Umfeld, das AI-, Cloud- und 5G-Infrastruktur der nächsten Generation ermöglicht

Klingt spannend?

Dann freuen wir uns auf Deine Bewerbung!
Werde Teil unserer Mission – für eine vernetzte, effiziente und nachhaltige digitale Zukunft.

Alle ausgewählten Kandidat:innen durchlaufen eine Hintergrundprüfung, um ein sicheres Arbeitsumfeld zu gewährleisten, Unternehmenswerte zu schützen und den gesetzlichen Anforderungen zu entsprechen.

nLighten steht für Chancengleichheit. Wir fördern ein diverses Arbeitsumfeld und freuen uns über Bewerbungen jeder Herkunft, jedes Geschlechts und jeder Identität – auch wenn Du nicht alle Kriterien erfüllst, freuen wir uns über Deine Bewerbung – insbesondere ermutigen wir Frauen und Menschen aus unterrepräsentierten Gruppen, sich bei uns zu bewerben.

title: Vendor & Contract Manager
description:
Company Profile

nLighten is a European platform of distributed edge data centers, designed to meet the growing demand for AI, 5G, and hybrid cloud deployments. As a rapidly expanding provider, we offer scalable colocation hubs and best-in-class energy solutions across Europe. Our innovative and sustainable approach to digital infrastructure ensures reliability, efficiency, and future-ready solutions for our clients. nLighten’s current footprint is 34 data centers in 7 European countries, with the ambition to grow to 100 sites during the next 3-4 years.

Learn more about us: www.nlighten.com

About the Role

We are seeking a Vendor & Contract Manager to take ownership of our repair, maintenance and cleaning operating cost across all 34 sites in 7 countries.

This is a new role within the central Facility function, reporting to the Head of Facility and working with a dotted line into Procurement. You will build the cost baseline, challenge what we buy and how often we buy it, consolidate fragmented contracts, and put supplier governance in place that holds.

The successful candidate will combine genuine technical competence in critical environments with the commercial rigour to lead vendor negotiations independently. This is not a procurement coordination role: you will be expected to read a maintenance scope, judge whether it is right, and defend that position with both the vendor and the business.

This role can be based in Germany or the Netherlands, with a European scope.

Key Responsibilities

R&M Operating Cost Ownership

• Own the repair, maintenance and cleaning operating cost across all 34 sites, building and maintaining a cost baseline by site, category and country

• Review, challenge and approve maintenance scopes before work is instructed, preventing unnecessary cost and scope creep

• Identify and eliminate duplicated services and inconsistent maintenance frequencies across the three legacy estates

• Deliver year-on-year reduction in operating cost per kW without reducing service outcomes, asset reliability or compliance

• Report monthly on spend, delivered savings, contract compliance and improvement initiatives, with every figure traceable to its source

Contract Management

• Own all hard and soft Facilities Management, statutory compliance and cleaning contracts across the portfolio, including mechanical and electrical maintenance, HVAC, UPS, generators, fire systems, BMS, water treatment, cleaning and security

• Lead contract renewals, competitive tenders and supplier negotiations to deliver commercial value and operational improvement

• Consolidate fragmented country-level contracts into pan-European agreements where consolidation is commercially justified

• Standardise scopes of work, contract terms and KPI frameworks across all countries

• Maintain a complete and accurate contract register covering cost, notice period, expiry and renewal status

• Implement supplier governance including KPI scorecards across safety, quality, responsiveness and commercial performance, periodic reviews, corrective action plans and clear escalation levels

• Develop category strategies and portfolio framework agreements for standard data-centre products such as racks, PDUs and cages

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Work with the Head of Facility on maintenance standards and the planned preventive maintenance programme, ensuring contracted scope matches the standard

• Work with Regional Directors and site teams so that contracted services meet real operational need at each site

• Maintain the dotted-line relationship with Procurement, and work with Finance and Legal on commercial terms, approvals and contract governance

• Travel regularly across our 7 countries and 34 sites as required

What We’re Looking For

• 5+ years managing multi-country hard and soft Facilities Management contracts, ideally in data centres or other mission-critical environments

• Track record of managing outsourced maintenance programmes and the vendor relationships behind them

• Proven ability to negotiate contracts and deliver measurable commercial savings

• Experience implementing supplier KPI and governance frameworks that changed vendor behaviour, not just reporting

• Strong working knowledge of data centre critical systems: power, cooling, UPS, generators and LV distribution

• Comfortable reading and reviewing technical documentation, method statements and maintenance scopes, and confident challenging what they contain

• Strong commercial acumen, able to challenge vendor pricing, scope and performance with confidence

• Practical command of contract structure: scope definition, service levels, notice and termination rights, indexation and exit terms

• Understanding of HSE, statutory compliance and contractor management

• Organised and process-driven, with a high standard for documentation and follow-through

• Clear, structured communicator, able to present technical and commercial information to senior stakeholders

• Collaborative style, able to influence across functions and geographies without direct authority

• Fluent in English; German, Dutch or French at professional working level is a strong advantage

Why Join Us?

• Join a fast-growing company shaping the future of digital infrastructure in Europe

• Take direct ownership of a new, high-visibility role at the centre of our Facility function

• Partner closely with the Head of Facility and Procurement, with real influence over how we spend and where

• Work in a dynamic environment with genuine autonomy and impact on measurable cost outcomes

• Be part of a collaborative team focused on operational excellence and sustainable growth

Apply now and be part of our journey toward a more connected, efficient, and sustainable digital future.

Background Check & Screening
All selected candidates will undergo a background check to ensure a safe workplace, protect company assets, and comply with regulations.

Diversity & Inclusion Statement
nLighten is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds. Even if you do not meet every requirement listed, we welcome your application. We particularly encourage women and individuals from underrepresented groups to apply.

title: Director, People & Culture
description:
ABOUT LAKEFIELD VETERINARY GROUP

We believe exceptional veterinary care starts with exceptional people. We partner with hospitals across the country to preserve what makes each practice special - its people, culture, and connection to community - while providing the operational support, resources, and strategic leadership that allow teams to thrive. As we grow, we remain committed to creating an environment where team members feel respected, supported, and empowered to deliver outstanding care.

Our Values

Our culture is built on five core values that guide us in the way we work:

• Respect

• Learning

• Do the right thing

• Wow service

• Fun

We expect all team members to actively demonstrate these values in their daily work and interactions.

Position Summary

The Director, People & Culture (P&C) serves as a trusted partner to business leaders and a key steward of Lakefield’s culture, team member experience, and people practices. This role is responsible for leading People Operations, Employee Relations, Benefits - Total Rewards, and our Regional HR Business Partner model while ensuring our hospitals receive consistent, practical, and people-centered support.

Success in this role requires balancing strategic thinking with hands-on execution, translating business needs into scalable people solutions that strengthen culture, drive consistency, and support organizational growth. The Director will spend meaningful time building relationships with hospital leaders and team members, developing a deep understanding of field operations and ensuring P&C remains closely connected to the realities of the business.

This leader succeeds by balancing a strong field orientation with operational excellence while creating the people processes, tools, and support structures that enable hospital leaders to focus on delivering exceptional patient care and team member experiences.

What you’ll do (Key Responsibilities)

People Operations & Compliance

• Lead People Operations, ensuring accurate and compliant administration of payroll, HR systems, policies, and employee lifecycle processes.

• Partner with Payroll and Finance teams to ensure timely, accurate payroll processing and continuous improvement to ensure data integrity and controls.

• Partner closely with the Chief People Officer on identifying workforce needs and developing practical solutions for our Operations and Medicine teams.

• Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local employment laws while balancing business needs and team member experience.

• Identify opportunities to streamline and strengthen people processes, creating consistency and scalability across a growing multi-state organization.

• Support Talent Acquisition processes and transactions.

Total Rewards

• Oversee administration of Lakefield's benefits programs, wellness offerings, leave programs, and employee experience initiatives.

• Oversee compensation and total rewards programs, including market benchmarking, pay practices, annual compensation planning, and employee communication.

• Evaluate program effectiveness and recommend enhancements that support attraction, retention, and engagement.

Employee Relations

• Serve as the organization's senior Employee Relations resource, providing guidance and consultation on complex workplace matters.

• Oversee investigations, performance management consultation, conflict resolution, policy interpretation, and workplace risk assessments.

• Coach field leadership through challenging people situations using sound judgment, consistency, and an understanding of each hospital's unique culture, team dynamics, and business needs.

• Promote a culture of accountability, respect, and trust while mitigating organizational risk.

Regional HR Business Partner Leadership

• Develop Lakefield's Regional HR Business Partner model at scale, in partnership with the Senior Manager, People & Culture, ensuring consistent support and partnership across hospitals and regions.

• Create the frameworks for coaching and the professional development of the HR Business Partners while establishing clear standards of service and partnership.

• Use data, trends, and field insights to proactively address organizational challenges and strengthen leader capability.

Culture & Field Partnership

• Champion Lakefield's culture and values through visible leadership, relationship-building, and active engagement with hospital teams.

• Maintain a regular presence in hospitals and field operations to understand team member experiences, support leaders, and ensure People & Culture remains closely connected to the business.

• Serve as a trusted advisor to leaders, helping navigate growth, change, and organizational challenges while preserving the unique cultures of our hospitals.

This list is not intended to be all-inclusive and may be modified as business needs evolve.

What we’re looking for

Required

• Bachelor's degree in human resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 10+ years of progressive Human Resources experience with increasing leadership responsibility.

• 5+ years leading one or more of the following functions: Employee Relations, HR Business Partners, People Operations, Benefits, Compensation, or Total Rewards.

• Experience supporting multi-site or geographically dispersed workforces.

• Demonstrated experience managing complex employee relations matters and workplace investigations.

• Experience leading HR programs and processes in a rapidly growing organization.

• Working knowledge of payroll administration, benefits programs, compensation practices, and employment law.

• Strong business acumen with the ability to connect people strategies to operational outcomes.

• Exceptional judgment, discretion, and problem-solving skills.

• Strong communication, coaching, and relationship-building capabilities.

• Ability to influence leaders through credibility, partnership, and practical solutions. 

 Preferred

• SHRM-SCP, SHRM-CP, SPHR, or PHR certification.

• Experience supporting healthcare, veterinary, retail, hospitality, or other service-based multi-location organizations.

• Experience building or leading HR Business Partner teams and field-based support models.

• Experience with ADP Workforce Now, Greenhouse, and other HR technology platforms.

• Experience supporting organizational growth, acquisitions, or change initiatives.

CORE COMPETENCIES

All Lakefield team members are expected to demonstrate:

• Strong communication skills (written and verbal)

• Collaboration across teams and functions

• Professional judgment and integrity

• Accountability and ownership of responsibilities

• Adaptability in a growing, evolving organization

• Alignment with Lakefield’s values

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position provides direct leadership, coaching, and development for the following P&C leaders:

• Senior Manager, People & Culture

• Manager, Total Rewards

• Manager, Payroll

WORK ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

This role operates in an office/hybrid environment with 3 days per week on-site at our office in Kent, WA. Physical requirements may include:

• Prolonged periods of sitting or standing

• Working at a computer

• Clinical exposure (if applicable)

TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS

Travel may be required up to 50% during the first 60 days of Onboarding to build relationships and gain an understanding of Lakefield's hospitals, operations, culture, and the veterinary industry. Ongoing travel is expected to be approximately 25%.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

The salary range for this position is between 170,000-190,000 annually.

Final compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, and internal equity. This position may also be eligible to participate in Lakefield’s annual incentive bonus program, subject to eligibility and plan terms.

Lakefield Veterinary Group offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k) with company match; paid time off; paid holidays; and additional wellness and development benefits.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Lakefield Veterinary Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all team members and applicants. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Regional Medical Director - Pacific Northwest (Oregon Predominant)
description:
Location: Pacific Northwest Region (Oregon predominant)

Position Summary:
The Regional Veterinary Medical Director is responsible for providing strategic medical leadership across multiple hospitals within an assigned region. This role ensures the highest standards of patient care, drives clinical excellence, and partners with hospital leadership to improve operational performance. The Regional Medical Director plays a critical role in mentoring veterinarians, strengthening hospital culture, and identifying opportunities for growth through data-driven insights and key performance indicators (KPIs).

Key Responsibilities:

Clinical Leadership & Patient Care

• Uphold and advance standards of veterinary medicine, ensuring high-quality, compassionate patient care across all hospitals.

• Promote best practices in veterinary medicine, including diagnostic approaches, treatment planning, and client communication

• Ensure compliance with all medical protocols, regulatory standards, and ethical guidelines.

• Demonstrate a working understanding of veterinary business operations, including workflow efficiency, patient flow, client experience, and financial awareness.

• Work with hospital medical directors and administrators in creating specific/strategic initiatives and monitor progress

• Provide direct mentorship and clinical guidance to early-career veterinarians, with a focus on building confidence and competency in general practice and surgery.

• Foster a positive culture and collaborative work environment promoting continuous learning, psychological safety, and teamwork.

Doctor Performance & Development

• Mentor, coach, and support veterinarians to enhance clinical skills, confidence, and professional growth with specific goals and timelines for mentee performance.

• Conduct performance evaluations and provide actionable feedback.

• Identify training needs and facilitate continuing education opportunities.

• Support recruitment, onboarding, and retention of veterinary talent.

Hospital Performance & Operational Excellence

• Partner with hospital leadership to oversee doctor productivity and overall hospital performance.

• Analyze KPIs (e.g., revenues, efficiency, case outcomes, client satisfaction, medical quality metrics) to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.

• Develop and implement strategic, data-driven plans to improve hospital performance and efficiency.

• Optimize hospital flow, including scheduling, workflow processes, and patient throughput.

• Drive consistency in medical and operational standards across locations.

Strategic Planning & Continuous Improvement

• Create and execute short- and long-term strategic plans for hospital growth and performance improvement.

• Identify inefficiencies and implement solutions to streamline operations and enhance patient care.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align medical initiatives with business objectives.

Leadership & Culture

• Promote a positive, collaborative, and inclusive hospital culture that reflects organizational values.

• Lead by example, fostering accountability, teamwork, and high engagement among staff.

• Provide effective leadership during times of change, growth, or operational challenges.

• Support conflict resolution and encourage open communication within teams.

Relationship Building

• Strengthen relationships with hospital leaders, veterinarians, and support staff.

• Serve as a trusted advisor and partner to regional and corporate leadership.

• Build strong connections with clients and the community to enhance trust and reputation.

Qualifications & Requirements:

• Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM or equivalent) required.

• Minimum of 5 years of clinical practice experience required.

• Active veterinary license in good standing (or ability to obtain licensure in the region).

• Leadership or multi-site oversight experience preferred.

• Willingness and ability to travel regionally on a regular basis.

Skills & Competencies:

• Strategic thinking and problem-solving

• Clinical excellence and medical judgment

• Leadership and team development

• Operational and financial acumen

• Communication and relationship-building

• Change management and adaptability

Work Environment & Travel:

• Regional travel will be necessary to support multiple hospital locations.

Compensation & Benefits

• The Salary range for this position will be $175k annually with 20% bonus potential.

• Lakefield offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k) with company match; paid time off; paid holidays; and additional wellness and development benefits. 

Impact of the Role:
This position plays a vital role in elevating medical quality, improving hospital performance, and fostering a culture of excellence. The Regional Veterinary Medical Director ensures that both patients and teams thrive, driving sustainable growth and exceptional care across the region.

About Lakefield Veterinary Group

We believe exceptional veterinary care starts with exceptional people. We partner with hospitals across the country to preserve what makes each practice special - its people, culture, and connection to community - while providing the operational support, resources, and strategic leadership that allow teams to thrive. As we grow, we remain committed to creating an environment where team members feel respected, supported, and empowered to deliver outstanding care.

title: Regional Medical Director - Washington
description:
Location: Washington State

Position Summary:

The Regional Medical Director (RMD) serves as a strategic medical leader and trusted partner to hospitals within their region. This role is responsible for supporting medical excellence, fostering collaborative hospital cultures, mentoring medical leaders, and helping practices achieve both clinical and operational success.

The RMD embraces innovation, relationship-building, and servant leadership. This position is highly collaborative and continuously evolving — success in the role is driven as much by mindset, adaptability, creativity, and emotional intelligence as by technical expertise. The RMD will have broad latitude to develop new ideas, support teams in meaningful ways, and help shape the future of medical excellence within Lakefield Veterinary Group.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Medical Leadership

• Provide strategic medical leadership and guidance to area hospitals.

• Help hospitals establish and advance a clear medical vision aligned with Lakefield’s values and standards of care.

• Collaborate with hospital medical teams to ensure Lakefield hospitals are recognized as outstanding within the veterinary profession.

• Work alongside hospital teams to identify strengths, opportunities for improvement, and pathways for continued growth.

• Provide strategic leadership to ensure high-quality medicine and patient care are consistently delivered across the region.

• Continually seek creative and innovative ways to improve hospital performance, culture, patient care, and team engagement.

Medical Team Support & Development

• Meet regularly — virtually and/or in person — with Medical Directors and hospital leadership teams throughout the region.

• Support hospitals with appropriate doctor, technician, and support staff utilization to maximize efficiency and patient care.

• Assist in developing medical leadership training programs, medical compliance training, and medical skill development initiatives.

• Help determine relevant educational material and topics for medical breakout sessions and regional training meetings.

• Support mentorship, coaching, and professional development for veterinarians and medical leaders.

• Help identify recruiting opportunities and participate in attracting and retaining top veterinary talent.

• Demonstrate a working understanding of veterinary business operations, including workflow efficiency, patient flow, client experience, and financial awareness.

Collaboration & Partnership

• Serve as an active participant and contributor to the Medical Advisory Board.

• Advocate for and help communicate medical initiatives, standards, and programs developed or approved by the Medical Advisory Board.

• Partner closely with Operations leadership to provide medical insight, support, and problem-solving.

• Support area hospitals in achieving annual practice objectives, goals, and strategic initiatives.

• Foster collaboration and knowledge-sharing among hospitals and teams across the region.

Industry Representation

• Represent Lakefield Veterinary Group professionally with industry leaders, vendors, veterinary organizations, and teaching institutions.

• Build strong relationships that support continued innovation, education, and excellence in veterinary medicine.

Culture & Engagement

• Assess and support a culture of continuous learning, psychological safety, and teamwork

• Serve as a role model for clinical excellence, professionalism, and compassionate care

• Find meaningful ways to recognize, celebrate, and support hospital teams and their accomplishments.

• Lead with empathy, accountability, and commitment to servant leadership.

Qualifications

• DVM or equivalent veterinary degree required.

• Active veterinary license in good standing; ability to obtain licensure in applicable states as needed.

• Minium of five years' experience in clinical veterinary practice.

• Minimum of two years in a leadership role within a practice.

• Strong clinical background with demonstrated leadership experience preferred.

• Excellent communication, mentorship, and relationship-building skills.

• Ability to influence and lead through collaboration rather than authority alone.

• Strategic thinker with strong problem-solving and organizational abilities.

• Passion for developing people, teams, and hospital culture.

• Comfortable with travel throughout the assigned region.

• Experience in multi-site or regional practice environments preferred.

Personal Attributes:

• Personable, approachable, and supportive

• Encouraging and motivating, with a genuine passion for developing others

• Collaborative mindset with a team-first attitude

• Committed to continuous improvement, both personally and professionally

Success Measures:

• Positive feedback from veterinarians and hospital teams.

• Measurable impact on hospital performance and patient care quality.

• Leadership development and collaboration with hospital leadership and teams

• Financial performance of hospitals in regions

• Individual performance

Travel Requirements

• Regular travel to regional hospitals required.

• Leading medicine and/or operational segments at Lakefield regional and national meetings,

• Representing Lakefield at leadership events, industry conferences, recruiting events, career fairs, or veterinary colleges as periodically requested.

Compensation & Benefits

• The Salary range for this position will be $150,000 - $175,000 annually. Final compensation will be determined by experience and qualifications.

• 20% Bonus opportunity for meeting performance parameters.

• Lakefield offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k) with company match; paid parental leave; paid time off; paid holidays; and additional wellness and development benefits.

Work Environment & Physical Requirements

This role operates in a hybrid environment. Physical requirements may include:

• Prolonged periods of sitting or standing

• Working at a computer

• Frequent automobile travel and periodic airplane travel

• Clinical practice and leadership working alongside associate doctors, medical directors, and hospital teams.

What Makes This Role Unique

This role is intentionally dynamic and evolving. The Regional Medical Director is not confined to a rigid set of responsibilities, but rather serves as a creative, strategic partner to hospitals and teams. Success in this position comes from embracing innovation, building trust, identifying opportunities, and continuously finding new ways to support teams and elevate patient care.

At Lakefield Veterinary Group, we value leaders who are collaborative, adaptable, forward-thinking, and passionate about making a meaningful impact on both people and pets.

As we grow, we remain committed to creating an environment where team members feel respected, supported, and empowered to deliver outstanding care.

title: Veterinary Hospital Area Manager
description:
Summary

The Veterinary Hospital Area Manager is accountable for driving sustainable growth, operational excellence, and regulatory compliance across a portfolio of veterinary hospitals. This role blends hands-on in-hospital leadership with data-driven management, ensuring adherence to company policies and operational standards while championing change initiatives, customer service, team development and strong cultural well-being. The Area Manager serves as the primary culture carrier for both Lakefield and the hospital, effectively balancing the legacy of the team with long-term growth opportunities to sustain a positive and balanced environment.

Reporting To: Regional Director of Operations

Direct Reports: Hospital Administrators / Practice Managers, potentially Client Service Leads

Travel: Regional travel between assigned hospitals. Occasional out-of-state travel to conferences or other leadership meetings may be required.

Schedule: Onsite in assigned hospitals a minimum of 4 days per week; availability for periodic evenings/weekends as needed during critical project initiatives or based on strategic needs. Occasional evenings/weekends for events, audits, or emergent needs.

Requirements: Must be currently residing in Oregon or willing to relocate. 3+ years of veterinary hospital or human healthcare experience.

Core Responsibilities:

Hospital Presence and Leadership

• Be present in assigned hospitals at least 4 days per week. Some visits require a structured agenda shared with the hospital leadership prior to the visit. Additional visits include listening to all levels of team members to gauge team culture and identify team members that may be at risk of leaving the company. Coaching hospital leadership and ensuring Lakefield’s policies are upheld.

• Conduct regular hospital walk-throughs, team huddles, one-on-ones with practice leadership as well as all team members, and attend team meetings at least twice a year per hospital needs.

• Build strong relationships with medical leadership to align operations with clinical standards.

Growth and Operational Performance

• Serve as a growth advocate: build and execute local market plans to increase new client acquisition, client retention, and revenue per visit.

• Coordinate team participation in community events – once per quarter from the Lakefield Marketing event worksheet.

• Optimize appointment templates and throughput while protecting quality of care and client experience.

• Manage hours of operation to balance client demand, staff coverage, and profitability.

• Partner with recruiting team on recruiting strategies and staffing models to support growth and service delivery. Actively recruit doctors and team members for assigned hospitals.

• Participate in annual budgeting process for each hospital.

Compliance and Policy Adherence

Ensure consistent execution of company policies, operational standards, and regulatory compliance across assigned hospitals. Key responsibilities include:

• Oversee compliance with company policies, OSHA standards, medical record requirements, scheduling practices, client service standards, and hours of operation.

• Monitor local marketing initiatives, new client acquisition efforts, and recruiting event participation to support hospital growth.

• Identify training needs, coordinate onboarding and leadership development, and support Hospital Administrator performance management.

• Champion adoption and optimization of the ezyVet practice management system while promoting standardized workflows across hospitals.

• Analyze key business metrics—including financial performance, KPIs, labor, production, client experience, and operational reports—to identify trends, drive continuous improvement, and implement corrective action plans.

• Develop, standardize, and maintain operational processes and SOPs to ensure consistency and efficiency across the region.

Data, Systems, and Process Improvement

• Run weekly KPI reviews: appointments, conversion, charge capture, compliance audit scores, labor vs. revenue, inventory turns, and client experience.

• Review and update (if applicable) financial information including PowerBI reports, Profit and Loss Statements, para labor reports, DVM production reports, Visit Volume reports

• Use ezyVet reporting and dashboards to identify trends and implement corrective action plans.

• Standardization of processes across hospitals; document SOPs and ensure version control and training.

People Leadership and Culture

• Coach Hospital Administrators and frontline leaders on performance management and accountability.

• Foster a culture of safety, empathy, and continuous improvement.

• Coordinate with Medical Directors to align operational goals with clinical quality initiatives.

• Support recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and retention efforts; coordinate engagement at recruiting events.

• Assist Hospital Administrators in performance coaching and disciplinary action when appropriate.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Partner with Marketing, HR, IT, Finance, Legal, and the Medical Advisory Board to execute initiatives.

• Serve as the voice of the hospital teams to TPC; escalate risks and resource needs promptly.

• Plan and facilitate regional meetings, training, and readiness checks for new rollouts.

Working Conditions

• Hybrid administrative work on the fifth day for reporting, planning, and follow-ups.

Qualifications

• 3+ years of multi-site operations management preferred, preferably in veterinary, medical, or similar healthcare services.

• Demonstrated experience driving growth and enforcing compliance in a regulated environment.

• Strong knowledge of OSHA requirements and healthcare documentation standards; veterinary-specific experience strongly preferred.

• Experience with practice management systems; ezyVet experience is a plus.

• Proven capability in change management, training, and coaching.

• Data-driven operator with proficiency in Excel/Sheets and dashboard tools.

• Excellent communication, conflict resolution, and stakeholder management skills.

title: Formation & Emploi - Technicien(ne) spécialisé(e) en infrastructures complexes
description:
Technicien·ne Spécialisé.e en Infrastructures Complexes (CVC) — Formation rémunérée + Alternance + perspective CDI
Localisation : Paris (Tremblay-en-France, AFORP) ou Marseille (La Plateforme / NRSud)
Type de contrat : POEI rémunérée (3 mois) + alternance (7 mois) — perspective CDI
Démarrage : rentrée septembre 2026
Durée totale : 10 mois (3 mois en centre + 7 mois en alternance entreprise)
Profil : titulaires d'un Bac Pro MELEC, toutes promotions confondues
Tu as ton Bac Pro MELEC ? On te forme et on te place sur les sites les plus exigeants de France.
Les datacenters et les sites industriels critiques recrutent en masse des techniciens spécialisés, celles et ceux qui maintiennent, dépannent et mettent en service les infrastructures qui font tourner Internet, l'industrie et l'énergie. C'est un métier qui ne connaît pas le chômage, qui paye bien, et qui ouvre des perspectives partout en France et à l'international.
Le hic : un Bac Pro seul ne suffit pas. Il manque les habilitations, la spécialisation CVC (Chauffage – Ventilation – Climatisation), la maîtrise des systèmes de supervision GTB/BMS, et l'expérience terrain.
On te propose un parcours de 10 mois pour combler tout ça — et décrocher un emploi durable.
Comment ça se passe
Phase 1 — De septembre à décembre 2026 : 3 mois de formation rémunérée (POEI, 399 heures)
Tu rejoins le centre à temps plein. La formation est prise en charge et rémunérée dans le cadre d'une Préparation Opérationnelle à l'Emploi (POEI). Au programme :
• Habilitations électriques BR, B1, H1 (passage à la fin de la séquence)

• Habilitations fluidiques (manipulation des fluides frigorigènes, brasure, recherche de fuite)

• Spécialisation Infrastructures Complexes : électricité courants forts, thermodynamique et froid, tuyauterie / fluides, mécanique, courants faibles, GTB/BMS (Schneider Ecostruxure), sûreté, maintenance, anglais technique

Phase 2 — De janvier à juillet 2027 : 7 mois en alternance rémunérée
Tu signes un contrat d'apprentissage ou de professionnalisation avec une entreprise partenaire, sur l'un des deux métiers ci-dessous (selon profil et opportunités) :
Option A — Installation et travaux CVC Monter, raccorder, tester et mettre en service les équipements thermoclimatiques sur des sites neufs ou en rénovation. Tu interviens en équipe, en lien avec les bureaux d'études et les sous-traitants.
Option B — Exploitation et maintenance CVC Assurer le bon fonctionnement quotidien des installations en service. Tournée de ronde, surveillance via GTB/BMS, maintenance préventive, diagnostic et intervention sur incident, reporting.
Rythme : 1 semaine en centre de formation / 3 semaines en entreprise. Rémunération sur toute la période.
Phase 3 — À l'issue : CDI envisageable
Plusieurs entreprises partenaires sont en demande active de techniciens formés sur ces métiers. Un CDI peut t'être proposé à la fin de l'alternance sur le même poste, dans la continuité directe.
À l'issue de la formation, tu sauras
• Lire et interpréter un schéma électrique, un plan P&ID, un synoptique GTB

• Identifier et nommer (en français et en anglais technique) tous les équipements d'un site critique : TGBT, UPS, groupes électrogènes, chillers, CRAC, CTA, dry coolers, baies serveurs…

• Manipuler les fluides frigorigènes en sécurité (charge, récupération, recherche de fuite)

• Diagnostiquer une panne, déclencher la bonne procédure et rédiger un rapport d'intervention

• Naviguer sur une supervision GTB/BMS, qualifier une alarme, intervenir en premier niveau

• Respecter les consignes de sécurité et de sûreté propres aux environnements critiques

Profil recherché
• Bac Pro MELEC validé — peu importe quand (2, 5 ou 10 ans, toutes les promotions sont les bienvenues)

• Bases solides en électricité (niveau Bac Pro MELEC) - testées lors d'une journée ou recommandées par un professeur

• Esprit orienté solutions, raisonnement logique

• Envie de travailler les mains dans le concret, sur des sites qui font tourner l'économie réelle

• Mobilité IDF (Tremblay-en-France) ou Sud (Marseille) selon le centre que tu choisis

Votre contexte de travail
La Plateforme
La Plateforme est la Grande école du numérique pour tous basée à Marseille avec plusieurs antennes en France. Cofondée avec le Club Top 20 réunissant les grandes entreprises de la Métropole Aix Marseille, l’école propose une offre de formations diversifiées et certifiantes dans le domaine de l’informatique et des technologies. La Plateforme_ est reconnue Établissement d’Enseignement Supérieur Technique Privé. La volonté de la Plateforme Créative est d’accueillir dans l’école à Marseille tous les publics, sans pré-requis de diplôme et sans conditions de ressources.
Le pôle jeunesse de la Plateforme conçoit et organise des ateliers pour les 12-18 ans pour favoriser des pratiques numériques créatives, saines et équilibrées, faire découvrir des métiers et susciter des vocations. Une attention particulière est portée sur les publics féminins et les jeunes issus des quartiers prioritaires. Le programme Cyberpark fait partie des activités du pôle Jeunesse et a été conçu avec le fonds de dotation Advens For People and Planet.
Le Fonds de dotation Advens for People and Planet créé en 2021 est le partenaire d’impact de l’entreprise Advens, experte en cybersécurité. Le fonds développe des initiatives visant à transformer la société et à renforcer le pouvoir d’agir individuel et collectif. C’est cette vision qui guide nos initiatives, régies en 3 grands piliers dont celui de l’éducation et de l'inclusion. Nous co-créons, finançons et déployons des projets à impact.
Nous sommes fermement convaincus que l’espace numérique commun de confiance est à construire ensemble et qu’il est vecteur d’apprentissage et d’insertion professionnelle durable.

Le programme Cyberpark
Le programme Cyberpark est un programme ludique pour les adolescent.e.s de 14 à 18 ans qui se déroule sur les temps extrascolaires principalement, et notamment pendant les vacances scolaires.
Dans un format de 2 jours, les adolescent.e.s participent à différents ateliers et jeux - dont un escape game - qui les sensibilisent aux usages sains et responsables du numérique et leur font découvrir la cybersécurité et les métiers liés.
Lancé en 2024 à Marseille, Cyberpark se déploie depuis juillet 2025 dans plusieurs villes de France, dont Lille.

Dans le cadre de ce déploiement, nous recherchons des animateur.rices sur Marseille, Lille et Ile-de-France.
Ces animateur.rice.s seront formé.e.s par nos équipes pour acquérir la méthode d'animation Cyberpark, et prendront ensuite leur poste de vacataire au sein d'un binôme d'animateur.rice.s. Ils seront managés par l'équipe pilote de Cyberpark.

Profil recherché

L'animateur.rice Cyberpark devra être doté.e :
- D’un talent pour l’animation (BAFA ou expérience significative obligatoire) : ll/elle sait accueillir et animer en toute sécurité un groupe d’adolescent.e.s, il /elle crée la dynamique de groupe, il/elle sait faire preuve de médiation et d’écoute, il/elle propose et participe à des jeux dans les temps de pause des ateliers et de repas.
- D’une appétence forte pour le numérique : il/elle devra animer les contenus des ateliers de Cyberpark. En plus de la formation qui sera délivrée par la Plateforme, il/elle montrera une réelle appétence pour le numérique de façon générale, et pour les problématiques de prévention numérique et de cybersécurité en particulier.

- D’une envie de transmettre et de s’engager : Cyberpark et plus largement notre école se donnent pour mission d’accompagner la jeunesse dans leur acculturation numérique, mais aussi de leur donner des outils pour développer leur confiance, notamment pour leur orientation. Cyberpark vise 50% de public en quartier prioritaire et 50% de jeunes filles. Notre animateur.rice a donc l’envie de s’engager dans un projet éducatif à impact.

Autres compétences

• Appétence pour le travail en équipe et pour l’apprentissage

• Adaptabilité

• Polyvalence

• Sens pédagogique & bienveillance

• Aisance relationnelle

• Patience et disponibilité

Vous êtes peut-être fait·e pour cette mission si vous avez :

description:
Aircall is a unicorn, AI-powered customer communications platform used by 22,000+ companies worldwide to drive revenue, resolve issues faster, and scale customer-facing teams. We’re redefining customer communications by bringing voice, SMS, WhatsApp, and AI together into one seamless workspace.

Our momentum comes from a simple idea: help teams work smarter, not harder. Aircall’s AI Voice Agent automates routine calls, AI Assist streamlines post-call work, and AI Assist Pro delivers real-time guidance so people can do their best work. The result is higher revenue, faster resolutions, and teams that scale with confidence.

Aircall is headquartered in Paris, our European HQ, with a strong North American presence anchored in Seattle, our North American HQ, and teams across Madrid, London, Berlin, San Francisco, New York City, Sydney, and Mexico City. We’ve built a product customers love and a business that’s scaling quickly, backed by world-class investors and driven by rapid AI innovation across multiple product lines.

At Aircall, you’ll join a company in motion. We’re ambitious, product-driven, and execution-focused, with visible impact, fast decisions, and real growth.

How we work at Aircall: We’re customer-obsessed, data-driven, and focused on delivering meaningful outcomes. We value ownership, continuous learning, and thoughtful speed. If you thrive in a collaborative, fast-moving environment where trust and impact matter, you’ll feel at home here.

About the Role:

We are seeking a highly motivated Small Business Account Executive to join our dynamic team which is focused on the North American market. The role itself is based in NYC.

As a Small Business Account Executive, you will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in the fast-paced world of B2B software sales.

This role will provide valuable insights into the sales process, customer relationship management and market research within the SaaS industry. This role offers an excellent learning opportunity to develop consultative sales skills and grow professionally for individuals interested in pursuing or continuing a career in sales.

This is an onsite role based in NYC, with an expectation of 3 days a week in office (Tuesday-Thursday).

Key Responsibilities:

• 
Guide prospects through our sales cycle while documenting all customer interactions (calls, emails, demos) in Salesforce

• 
Use a consultative selling approach (SPICED): Uncover pain points and help prospects realize Aircall’s value through conversational discovery calls & tailored demos

• 
Work collaboratively with other teams (Sales Development, Onboarding, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Support) to drive opportunities across the finish line

• 
Accurately forecast new revenue each week, month, and quarter by keeping pipeline up to date within Salesforce

Qualifications:

• 
6+ months of closing experience in the Small Business/Mid-Market sector

• 
Consistent attainment (and overachievement) of quota and revenue goals in a high-volume, transactional sale

• 
Experience in a fast-paced environment with many competing priorities: An ability to stay organized and efficiently manage your time

• 
Familiarity with SPICED Sales Methodology & ability to challenge prospects & status quo

• 
Ability to articulate technical components of a product in a simple and effective manner (Selling Aircall requires a deep product knowledge. Learning these functions and clearly expressing their value is what this role is all about)

• 
An eagerness to become a product expert, understanding how customers are using Aircall and Aircall’s dozens of powerful software integrations

• 
You’re a driven, goal-oriented team player with a “must-win” attitude: we win and lose as a team

• 
The willingness to learn and be coached! Our product, sales processes, team, and company will continue to evolve and there is always more to learn

• 
You learn from failure: We’re risk-takers. Trying, succeeding, failing — and trying again — are essential to who we are as a team and company

• 
You’re resourceful and scrappy: you will figure out what you need quickly to get the job done and get the deal across the finish line. You don’t wait for answers to come to you, you go out and find answers

• 
A desire to grow within the AE role for 2-3 years minimum. This is a long-term role with plenty of room for individual development (and significant earning potential!)

• 
Spanish speaking is a plus

Why join us?

🚀 Key moment to join Aircall in terms of growth and opportunities

💆‍♀️ Our people matter, work-life balance is important at Aircall

📚 Fast-learning environment, entrepreneurial and strong team spirit

As an Account Manager at Aircall, you are the owner of customer success and revenue growth across your portfolio. Acting as both the voice of Aircall for the customer and the voice of the customer within Aircall, you ensure our customers realize the full value of their investment while fueling sustainable growth for Aircall.

By deeply understanding the needs of our customers across a variety of industries and use cases, you become the trusted expert who identifies growth potential and helps improve the customer experience. This means translating customer goals into solutions that unlock adoption, value realization, and expansion — ensuring each account grows in both impact and partnership over time.

This is a highly strategic and commercial role — blending consultative relationship management with the rigor and energy of a quota-carrying seller. You’ll partner cross-functionally with Customer Engineering, Product, and Support to accelerate adoption, drive usage of add-on SKUs, and build deep, long-term relationships with customers at all levels of their organizations.

Aircall is undergoing an exciting transformation — building on our market-leading communications platform and introducing AI functionality that helps customers operate more intelligently, efficiently, and competitively. Join us and be part of shaping that journey.

This is a hybrid role, in office 3 days a week in Paris.

Key Responsibilities:

• Own NRR: Manage the full post-sale lifecycle — driving renewals, expansions, and churn mitigation to deliver predictable and profitable growth.

• Drive Growth: Identify and activate growth opportunities within your portfolio, prospecting into new subsidiaries, use cases, and additional SKUs to unlock untapped potential.

• Target Strategically: Prioritize high-potential accounts that may have low spend today but represent strong expansion opportunities, developing long-term growth plans.

• Prospect and Outbound: Run proactive outreach within your base to expand relationships and identify new value creation opportunities.

• Develop Stakeholder Maps: Build and maintain multi-layer relationships — from daily users to senior decision-makers — ensuring alignment, sponsorship, and retention.

• Sell Competitively: Position Aircall’s value head-to-head against competitors, with a clear understanding of how our solutions address each customer’s unique business needs.

• Negotiate and Close: Lead complex renewal and upsell negotiations, balancing commercial outcomes with customer success to close revenue and foster loyalty.

• Manage Pipeline & Forecast: Maintain an accurate pipeline of renewal and expansion opportunities and deliver consistent, data-driven NRR forecasting.

• Partner for Adoption: Collaborate closely with your Customer Engineering counterpart to ensure customers achieve adoption milestones and measurable outcomes.

• Champion the Customer Voice: Surface insights, pain points, and product feedback that inform Aircall’s product roadmap and go-to-market strategies.

• Shape Local Strategy: Share learnings across teams to enhance customer experience and strengthen regional growth initiatives.

Qualifications: 

• Experienced in SaaS Account Management, Commercial Customer Success, or Renewal Management, with a track record of achieving revenue targets.

• Skilled in consultative sales, prospecting, and negotiation, with the ability to balance commercial focus and customer advocacy.

• Customer-obsessed — curious about how different industries and use cases leverage Aircall, and proactive in identifying ways to add value.

• Capable of developing and executing account expansion strategies, including stakeholder mapping and whitespace analysis.

• Confident in competitive sales cycles, able to articulate differentiation and handle objections effectively.

• Analytical, detail-oriented, and accountable for forecast accuracy and pipeline hygiene.

• Resilient, driven, and passionate about helping customers realize long-term value through partnership.

• Excited by innovation and transformation — particularly the opportunity to represent a next-generation AI-powered communications platform.

At Aircall, you’ll join a fast-moving, customer-obsessed team that thrives at the intersection of success and growth. Customer Engineers (CEs) are the technical drivers of customer success at Aircall. They ensure that what we sell becomes what customers use — and what they use becomes what they grow.
CEs own the onboarding, activation, and technical adoption journey, ensuring every customer realises measurable value from Aircall’s platform.
They combine deep product and integration expertise with strong communication skills, structured project management, and commercial awareness. This is a customer-facing, proactive, and high-impact role — designed for those who can translate complex technology into clear outcomes and act as trusted advisors from implementation through expansion.

*Unfortunately candidates without the right to work in Australia cannot be considered at this time 

Key Responsibilities

1. Own Customer Activation

You’ll lead the technical onboarding for new customers - configuring integrations, enabling features, and guiding them to first value with confidence and clarity. Your goal: fast, frictionless activation and a confident go-live experience that sets the foundation for long-term success.

2. Drive Adoption and Growth

Beyond launch, you’ll help customers unlock the full potential of Aircall. You’ll monitor product usage, identify adoption opportunities, and host enablement sessions or office hours to deepen engagement. You’ll ensure customers understand - and use - the capabilities that make a real impact, including our AI-driven features. This might require supporting our customers in building or owning the implementation of advanced services with low-code solutions or scripts on the basis of a professional services catalog.

3. Manage Renewals and Value Realization

In close partnership with Account Managers, you’ll bring a technical lens to the renewal process. You’ll validate system health, ensure adoption goals are met, and demonstrate ROI through clear value metrics. Your partnership helps ensure customers renew confidently, knowing Aircall powers measurable outcomes.

4. Lead Add-On Activations

When customers purchase new modules - such as AI Assist Pro or advanced analytics -  you’ll oversee the setup and activation, ensuring features are properly configured, adopted, and delivering value from day one.

5. Proactively Monitor and Support Your Portfolio

Each week, you’ll review customer health signals, product telemetry, and usage trends. You’ll reach out before issues arise — to coach, consult, and prevent risk — ensuring every customer feels guided, not reactive.

When critical or tactical issues surface, you’ll act as the project manager - coordinating Support, Product, and Engineering to ensure a fast, transparent resolution. You’ll handle a handful of structured escalations each quarter and use those moments to strengthen trust and process maturity.

Strong project management and stakeholder alignment skills; capable of driving accountability on both sides.

• 
Understands how technical adoption connects to revenue — renewals, expansions, and customer advocacy.

• 
Partners seamlessly with AMs, ensuring data-driven insight feeds into renewal and upsell planning.

• 
Comfortable contributing to value discussions and supporting commercial conversations with factual adoption data.

Collaboration & Influence

• 
Works fluidly across SE, AM, Support, and Product functions.

• 
Acts as the connective tissue between technical delivery and business outcomes.

• 
Brings solutions, not just escalations — always seeks to simplify and improve.

• 
4–8 years or more in a customer-facing technical role (Customer Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Implementation Specialist, or similar).

Proven experience leading SaaS implementations and driving product adoption in mid-market or enterprise environments.

Strong technical background: API integrations, cloud tools, or customer data platforms.

Build and run a new AI Ops capability that embeds AI into the daily workflows of SDRs, BDRs, AEs, PAMs, etc. — from prospecting and call intelligence to next-best-action, forecasting, and pipeline hygiene. • 
Partner across the RevOps function. Work hand in hand with Customer Ops (AM Ops, CE Ops, FDE Ops, SE Ops, Support Ops) on land-and-expand and retention motions, and with Revenue Planning & Insights (planning, analytics, PMO, commissions) on targets, capacity, territory and quota design, comp plans, and reporting — so acquisition and customer motions operate as one system.

Build the systems and single source of truth. Partner with Data and GTM Systems to ensure the tooling, data architecture, and dashboards behind acquisition and AI Ops are clean, scalable, and trusted by leadership and the field alike.

Shift the perception of RevOps. Move RevOps from a function that controls the business to one that demonstrably helps it grow — earning the right to lead through reliability, insight, and impact.

• 
A track record of operationalizing AI or new tooling for field sellers — not just evaluating tools, but driving adoption, building workflows, and proving productivity impact at scale.

• 
Strong systems and data fluency; comfortable partnering with Data and Systems teams on architecture, reporting, and a trustworthy single source of truth (Salesforce and the broader GTM stack).

Excellent cross-functional leadership and stakeholder management; you can align a CRO, GMs, Finance, and operations peers around one operating model and hold the line on consistency.

A builder's bias: you turn ambiguity into repeatable process and structure, and you genuinely enjoy making large GTM teams run better.
